scores.evidence: The two-column table dr-table stays readable at 390 px (pages/mobile-jp-03.png, mobile-jp-04.png). The flowchart TD cycle-flow has short JP labels and a readable feedback loop, '直す指摘がある' (mobile-jp-17.png, desktop-jp-11/12.png). The highlighted lines of the settings code blocks (ex-settings, setup-settings-model) are easy to tell apart, and line 16 soft-wraps legibly under its own line number (mobile-jp-09.png).

No screen is text-only (textOnlyScreens empty), and headings, steps, quizzes and figures alternate steadily. The example section stacks ex-steps, ex-prompt-claude-md, ex-settings and ex-prompt-skill back to back, which is about 5 mobile screens of steps, prompt and code (mobile-jp-06 to 11.png). The prerequisites line at the top is a dense 10-item run of text (mobile-jp-01.png).

All visible text is Japanese with English glosses where intended, the diagram labels are in JP, contrast is good, and no control is hidden under the bars. There are a few awkward breaks: a line that starts with '、' before the chip `.claude/skills/` in ex-share (mobile-jp-07.png), a lone 'す' in q2 option 1 and a lone 'く' in e1 option 3 on desktop (desktop-jp-08.png, desktop-jp-17.png), and 'git' / 'push' split across lines in the sc-safety label (mobile-jp-22/23.png).

niceToHave: self-check-list (sc-safety): put git push in a code chip, as in 「`git push` の確認ルール」, so the two words stay on one line at 390 px (pages/mobile-jp-22.png shows 'git' and 'push' on separate lines).

check-quiz e1 option a and ex-quiz q2 option a: on desktop these are the only options that wrap, each leaving one character alone on the second line ('置/く', '足/す'). This makes the correct answer stand out visually as the longest option. Shorten them slightly, for example 「テストのコマンドはCLAUDE.md、鍵は拒否ルール、pushは確認ルールへ」 (pages/desktop-jp-17.png, pages/desktop-jp-08.png).

ex-steps (ex-share): the line starts with '、' after the chip `.claude/settings.json` (pages/mobile-jp-07.png). Rewording as 「CLAUDE.mdと `.claude/settings.json` と `.claude/skills/` をコミットします。」 avoids the kinsoku break.
Example section: consider moving ex-prompt-skill after ex-quiz, or merging prompts, to break up about 5 mobile screens of steps, prompt and code (pages/mobile-jp-06.png to mobile-jp-11.png).
reader: desktop charsPerLine median is 42, above the JP target of 30–40 (measure 680 px); this is a reader layout setting, not lesson content.
reader: the keys row for c-plan shows 'Shift + Tab' and 'Ctrl + G' next to each other with no visible separator, so it can read as a single four-key combo (pages/mobile-jp-18.png, desktop-jp-12.png).
reader: step p-more has only a hint, but its expander is labelled 'うまくいかないときは' (pages/mobile-jp-13.png).
reader: the prerequisites line renders as one long run of text separated by '、' (pages/mobile-jp-01.png); a list or a collapsible would help.
reader: the end banner says this is the course's last lesson because drafts are not in course.json (pages/mobile-jp-30.png); this is a known preview behaviour.
summary: No hard failures in metrics.json: no overflow, console errors, mermaid errors, unknown blocks or broken images. No personal data appears on any screen. The table, flowchart and highlighted settings code are all readable at 390 px, and wrapped code lines and chips stay easy to follow. The remaining issues are minor Japanese line-break orphans and a dense run of blocks in the example section, all listed as nice-to-have.
